Managing Handicaps going forward

Option 1: OPTION 1 — Rolling Placings Adjustment (Very Simple, Very Robust)
  • Each week, adjust handicaps based on how far someone finished from the “target placing”, e.g. 5th.
  • ||(\Delta handicap = (actual\_placing - target\_placing) \times step\_size||)
  • Step size can be 2 or 5 second increments.
  • Can clamp adjustments (e.g max 10 seconds per week to avoid huge swings)
  • NOTE: this is different from what we've done because we have a target range of places (5-10), rather than a target single place (5).
  • Pros
    • Extremely simple
    • Easy to explain
    • Self-correcting
    • Works well with irregular attendance
  • Cons
    • Doesn't consider field strength on the day
    • Top athletes in weak fields may still dominate temporarily
Option 2: Percentile-Based Adjustment (More Fair with Variable Field Sizes)
  • Use a target percentile (e.g. 0.66 is top third) rather than target placing.
  • Improves Option 1 by normalizing for heat size.
  • ||(\delta handicap = (percentile - target_percentile) \times K||)
  • K is a tuning constant (e.g. 10 seconds).
  • Pros
    • Accounts for different heat sizes
    • Still simple
    • More statistically fair
  • Cons
    • Slightly harder to explain
    • Still Doesn't consider field strength on the day
Option 3: “Top-5 Frequency” Control System
  • Each athlete should finish top-5 about X% of the time (say 50%) in their last ||(M||) races (track races for each athlete individually).
  • Example:
    • More the 60% of last ||(M||) races in top 5, then increase handicap
    • Within 30%-60% of last ||(M||) races in top 5, then don't change handicap
    • Below 30%, then decrease handicap
  • Works well because:
    • Strong athletes still get wins
    • But domination is automatically corrected
    • Poor performance with large handicap gets fixed
  • Pros
    • Matches your fairness goals exactly
    • Resistant to random bad weeks
    • Attendance-friendly (looks at each athlete's last ||(M||) races)
  • Cons
    • Slower to react
Option 4: Separate "Fast Group" with smaller second steps
  • Above a certain ability level:
    • Handicaps increase more slowly
  • Example:
    • Normal athletes: ±5 seconds per step
    • Top 10% athletes: ±2 seconds per step
  • Rationale:
    • Keeps elite athletes competitive
    • Prevents runaway handicaps
    • Encourages continued participation
Option 5: Hybrid Formulaic and Judgment approach
  • Use Option 1 or 2 (Rolling placing adjustements) then periodically review manually (every month)
  • During review:
    • Identify athletes who:
      • Have a large handicap
      • Are never top-5
    • Reduce handicap manually (even if math says otherwise)
    • Also:
      • Cap handicaps within reasonable min/max bounds
      • Apply “gut checks” for obvious outliers
    • Rules of thumb
      • Never change a handicap by more than ~10-15% at once
      • Prefer many small nudges over big jumps
      • Transparency matters more than precision

Recommendation

  • Weekly adjustment
    • Use Percentile-based (Option 2) with small step sizes
  • Monthly review
    • Apply Option 3 logic for obvious unfairness
  • Hard limits
    • Min/max handicaps per event
  • Human override
    • If someone has a big handicap and is still bottom-half -> reduce it
This balances:
  • Fairness
  • Simplicity
  • Transparency
  • Fun
